inspection_summary: All 1,494 splitlines were inspected. The text layer preserves the article's prose, section structure, and most displayed formulas well enough to recover a linked chain from Farey-point discrepancy through Möbius-convolution criteria, short-interval residue decompositions, Kubert-function averaging, and the generalized-Dedekind-sum derivation of Franel's formula. Control-character placeholders and flattened notation make exact formula transcription unsafe in several displays, so formula-dependent units require consultation of the page image before downstream exact use.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines Farey series and discrepancies, recalls classical RH criteria, motivates Farey error sums, explains parity, and announces the paper's three contributions.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Preliminaries
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces Bernoulli power-sum machinery, Möbius-convolution sums S_s, their RH equivalence, and the transform from Farey sums to arithmetic convolutions.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Power moments
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives general Bernoulli expansions for Farey power moments and reduces quadratic and cubic whole-interval moment criteria to S(x).

sections_inspected.label: 4. Short interval results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Centers partial Farey sums, develops telescoping residue-class criteria, proves half-, third-, and quarter-interval RH equivalents, and records a centering obstruction.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Kubert functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses the Kubert distribution identity and parity structure to turn Farey averages of polylogarithmic, Bernoulli, Clausen, and logarithmic functions into RH-equivalent arithmetic sums.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Franel's theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates Bernoulli correlations to generalized Dedekind sums, proves their three-term relation, and derives Franel's discrepancy-square identity.

sections_inspected.label: References and author matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography, affiliations, and receipt date; no new mathematical argument.

accepted_units.title: Farey sequence construction and discrepancy coordinates
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the ordered reduced fractions, mediant insertion, cardinality scale, and the pointwise discrepancy delta_nu from uniform spacing that the later criteria measure.
accepted_units.context_note: Self-contained introductory setup; the concrete F_2 to F_3 example is illustrative rather than required.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Fraction subscripts and the Phi asymptotic are flattened but recoverable from prose; verify displays before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Mertens and Chebyshev formulations of RH
accepted_units.why_material: Records the two arithmetic error estimates that later Farey and Kubert identities reduce to, making explicit the downstream equivalence target.
accepted_units.context_note: The preceding lines identify RH; this span defines M and psi and states both equivalences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Superscripts in the O(x^(1/2+epsilon)) bounds are text-layer flattened but legible.

accepted_units.title: Uniform distribution reframed as a discrepancy-error program
accepted_units.why_material: Moves from equidistribution of Farey points to the stronger question of estimating test-function errors, explicitly proposing broad function classes as a route to RH criteria.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the interval-count asymptotic, Weyl-limit statement, full and short error definitions, and the paper's methodological motivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Integral and summation limits are flattened but their roles are stated in adjacent prose.

accepted_units.title: Parity-guided short-interval and Kubert criteria
accepted_units.why_material: Connects reflection parity to cancellation or interval reduction and states the paper's third- and quarter-interval and even-Kubert RH-equivalent estimates.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. The span is an overview and relies on the preceding discrepancy motivation and later definitions of h, S, and K_s.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several fractions, Bernoulli symbols, and displayed sums are flattened; the prose-supported parity and criterion claims are recoverable, while exact formulas need page-image verification.

accepted_units.title: Möbius-convolution sums as a zero-free-region detector
accepted_units.why_material: Defines S_s as a Dirichlet convolution and shows that square-root cancellation in S_s is equivalent to RH through the quotient zeta(z+s)/zeta(z) and its analytic continuation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definition, generating Dirichlet series, partial-summation integral, and converse from the Mertens bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Dirichlet-series quotient and integral are readable but typographically flattened; exact exponents should be checked.

accepted_units.title: Farey sums converted to Möbius convolutions
accepted_units.why_material: Provides the central reusable transform: a function summed over reduced fractions in an interval becomes a Möbius convolution with unrestricted numerator sums.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof explicitly removes coprimality by inserting the divisor sum for the Möbius function; the corollary specializes to interval counts.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Index substitutions remain recoverable, though some sigma and fraction layout is flattened.

accepted_units.title: Bernoulli decomposition of short-interval power moments
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the Farey-to-convolution transform with the Bernoulli power-sum formula to decompose every power moment into a uniform main term and structured arithmetic errors.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is short but depends on Lemmas 1 and 3, both retained in the inspected context.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The multi-line coefficient formula has extraction risk; retain the conceptual decomposition and verify coefficients against the page image.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic and cubic moments collapse to the same RH signal
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that distinct whole-interval power-moment deviations are affine multiples of S(x), hence equivalent to RH by a common hidden arithmetic statistic.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the general whole-interval corollary and the k=2 and k=3 specializations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moment exponents and constants are flattened but the reductions to S(x) are legible; exact constants need verification.

accepted_units.title: Centering a partial Farey sum by its local count
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces a fixed uniform center with h(xi)/(2 Phi(x)) and isolates the Bernoulli and S(x) terms that govern short-interval criteria.
accepted_units.context_note: This proposition is the algebraic setup used by Theorem 1 and the carried short-interval units.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed identity is formula-dependent and contains flattened fractions; verify exact coefficients before use.

accepted_units.title: Residue extraction and telescoping preserve cancellation exponents
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that removing multiples of a modulus and comparing scaled arguments can be inverted by a finite telescoping series, so the transformed bound is equivalent to the original S_s or Chebyshev bound.
accepted_units.context_note: The odd-part identity is the modulus-two case; the general N and c formulation supports the third- and quarter-interval criteria.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The sign convention in the telescoping displays is extraction-sensitive; the finite O(log x) inversion argument is clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Fractional-part kernel for centered short-interval Farey sums
accepted_units.why_material: Expresses the centered partial sum through a bounded fractional-part kernel weighted by the Mertens function, exposing the arithmetic channel behind all subsequent special intervals.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. Its proof substitutes the local-count estimate into Proposition 2, so lines 437-518 supply important setup.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definition of T(xi,x) is legible but control-character loss affects brackets; exact transcription requires the page image.

accepted_units.title: Local centering differs from cumulative Farey discrepancy only by bounded error
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies the explicit centering error, notes why it likely cannot be improved to o(1), and bridges the new centered sum to Landau's maximal-discrepancy RH criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument uses the identity between rank sums and h(xi), then invokes the stated Landau criterion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed maximum and cumulative sums are flattened but the comparison is explained in prose.

accepted_units.title: Half- and third-interval RH criteria
accepted_units.why_material: Specializes the fractional-part kernel at rational endpoints, turning centered Farey sums on one-half and one-third intervals into transformed S(x) expressions equivalent to RH.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. The one-third proof continues through line 693 and is recorded as a context repair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Constants and the scaled S(x/3) term are formula-text sensitive; the stated equivalences and parity explanation remain recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Modulo-three decomposition of the one-third kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Demonstrates how a rational interval endpoint converts the fractional-part kernel into a nonzero-residue sum and then uses the telescoping lemma to recover an RH-equivalent bound.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the omitted proof context for the one-third part of the carried u03.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Residue conditions are legible; exact numerical coefficients should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Quarter-interval RH criterion via odd residue classes
accepted_units.why_material: Derives a still shorter interval criterion by decomposing the kernel modulo four and reducing it to odd-part S sums whose estimate is equivalent to RH.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. The proof invokes the earlier telescoping lemma with N=2 and c=2/3.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The central displayed formula has flattened fractions and superscripts; exact coefficients require page-image verification.

accepted_units.title: Why fixed endpoint centering leaves uncontrolled residue sums
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that replacing the adaptive count h(xi) by naive constants at one-third or one-quarter introduces single-residue Mertens sums the authors do not know how to control.
accepted_units.context_note: This negative result distinguishes the successful centered criteria from a superficially simpler but unsupported formulation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Congruence classes are readable; the equalities' exact coefficients are extraction-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Kubert functions form a parity-split two-dimensional space
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the distribution identity, records the even/odd basis structure, identifies polylogarithm and Hurwitz-zeta realizations, and explains extension to the circle.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the semantic setup for selecting which function components survive symmetric Farey averaging.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Kubert identity and special-function series are flattened but recognizable; exact domains and normalizations should be checked.

accepted_units.title: Kubert identities turn Farey averages into gcd-weighted sums
accepted_units.why_material: Transforms single and pairwise Farey averages of a Kubert function into Mertens-weighted gcd sums, combining distribution identities with the Farey Möbius transform.
accepted_units.context_note: Parts (i) and (ii) and their proofs expose the mechanism; the logarithmic special case begins afterward.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The gcd exponent and normalization in the displays are formula-sensitive and require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The logarithmic Kubert function recovers Chebyshev's function
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a roots-of-unity product and divisor expansion of log m to identify the Farey sum of log|2 sin(pi x)| with psi(x), directly connecting a semantic function identity to a classical RH error term.
accepted_units.context_note: This proves Proposition 3(iii) and supplies a concrete instance of the general averaging transform.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Product and divisor-sum layouts are flattened, but the factorization-to-Chebyshev chain is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Bernoulli and polylogarithm averages share the S_s channel
accepted_units.why_material: Specializes the Kubert transform to Bernoulli polynomials and polylogarithms and relates a pairwise polylogarithm average to squared Farey discrepancy, foreshadowing Franel's identity.
accepted_units.context_note: The span collects the corollary's single-sum and pairwise-difference consequences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several constants and exponents are densely displayed and extraction-sensitive; verify exact formulas.

accepted_units.title: Non-odd Kubert components yield RH-equivalent Farey sums
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that a Kubert sum is a nonzero scalar multiple of S_{s-1}(x) precisely when the function has a surviving even component, making odd cancellation an explicit obstruction rather than a failure of the arithmetic criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes polylogarithm, general non-odd K_s, and Hurwitz-zeta formulations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The basis coefficients and parameter exclusions are legible; exact analytic hypotheses should be checked against the page image.

accepted_units.title: Fourier decomposition transfers Kubert criteria to Bernoulli and Clausen functions
accepted_units.why_material: Uses real and imaginary parts of polylogarithms to express the same RH signal in Bernoulli-polynomial and Clausen-function representations.
accepted_units.context_note: The recursive Clausen definitions and Fourier expansion make the transfer mechanism explicit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Integral signs, parity indices, and constants are flattened; the equivalence family is clear but exact normalizations need verification.

accepted_units.title: Half-interval tangent sums encode a Chebyshev scale difference
accepted_units.why_material: Converts a half-interval Farey sum of log tan into psi(x)-psi(x/2), whose square-root error is equivalent to RH by the estimate-preserving telescoping principle.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof combines finite tangent products with the Farey Möbius transform; a cotangent analogue is stated.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The product displays and constants have formula risk, though the Chebyshev difference is legible.

accepted_units.title: Generalized Dedekind correlations and their cyclic three-term law
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the Bernoulli correlation needed for Farey discrepancies and states the cyclic three-term relation whose gcd terms ultimately collapse to Franel's formula.
accepted_units.context_note: Lemma 7 links Farey Bernoulli products to these sums; Lemma 8 states the key relation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The three-term formula is densely typeset and flattened; its structural cyclic form is recoverable, but exact gcd coefficients require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Bernoulli identities and congruence counting prove the three-term law
accepted_units.why_material: Adapts a pointwise Bernoulli identity, sums it over congruence classes, and evaluates exceptional integral cases to turn analytic-looking correlations into gcd data.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose identifies the substitutions and case split even where displays are difficult; this is a reusable local-to-global proof pattern.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula density, control-character loss, and flattened cases make exact reuse unsafe without the page image.

accepted_units.title: Farey discrepancy squares become Bernoulli correlation sums
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites each discrepancy using the fractional-part Bernoulli function, expands its square, and isolates a double Mertens-weighted Bernoulli correlation to which Lemma 7 applies.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the first conceptual step in the proof of Franel's theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Normalization constants and summation indices are formula-sensitive; the expansion strategy is clear.

accepted_units.title: Cyclic averaging exposes the Dedekind three-term relation
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces a triple sum, observes its invariance under cyclic permutation, and averages the three presentations so Lemma 8 can replace Dedekind terms by symmetric gcd expressions.
accepted_units.context_note: The symmetrization is the decisive representation change in the Franel derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: An extraction artifact appears near line 1345 and the large display is flattened; verify all coefficients and subscripts.

accepted_units.title: Gcd and Möbius convolutions collapse the symmetrized expression
accepted_units.why_material: Evaluates the remaining symmetric gcd terms and a primitive-triple sum, reducing the three-variable expression to Phi(x) and completing Franel's exact identity.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the terminal simplification after the conceptual Dedekind-sum step.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Nested sums are heavily flattened; the stated reductions are recoverable, but exact algebra requires scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A common Farey-to-arithmetic transform
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Removing coprimality by Möbius inversion and then applying a function's distribution identity is the recurring mechanism that converts geometric Farey averages into classical arithmetic error sums.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The synthesis is internal to the displayed transforms here and does not establish that arbitrary test-function families admit a useful arithmetic reduction.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Parity and residue classes select informative intervals
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Reflection symmetry kills odd whole-interval components, while rational endpoint residue decompositions and invertible telescoping recover the same cancellation signal on selected shorter intervals.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Only the half-, third-, and quarter-interval mechanisms proved in this source are supported; naive fixed centering leaves uncontrolled residue sums.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Many criteria factor through one S_s statistic
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Power moments and several Kubert special-function averages are not independent RH signals here: each becomes a scalar or affine expression in the same Möbius-convolution family S_s.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Equivalence is established under the source's parameter and parity hypotheses, not for all moments or all special functions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Franel's formula as a chain of representation changes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Farey discrepancies are converted to Bernoulli correlations, then to generalized Dedekind sums, cyclically symmetrized, and finally collapsed by gcd/Möbius identities; the formula's origin is this representation chain rather than a direct discrepancy calculation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact coefficients are unsafe in the extracted text and must be checked against the source page image before formal or computational use.

within_source_saturation: Saturated for semantic segmentation: every section and proof-bearing range was inspected, all distinct mechanisms and the explicit failed simplification were represented, and unselected text is setup, repeated advance summary, whitespace/page matter, or bibliography. Further units would mainly split algebraic details already represented or rely on formula typography that the normalized text does not preserve safely.
